summary: Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and sinologist who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held faculty positions at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1982, 1985) and served as Professor of History at the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia C. Stanley was a scholar of linguistics and indology who earned her B.A. at the University of Chicago and her Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin. She taught at Washington State, Texas at Austin, Texas at El Paso, and the University of Łódź (1976–1978).

Patricia Fister is a specialist in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas. She worked at the Spencer Museum of Art, New Orleans Museum of Art, and served as professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2007–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a sinologist and Tibetologist who completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.

Patrick McAllister is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser, Karin Preisendanz, and Ernst Steinkellner. He has held research posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, Thomas Burrow, and R. C. Zaehner, and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University Bloomington (1974–1991) and UT Austin.

Patrick Pranke is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, under Robert E. Buswell Jr.
Patrick Robert Cadell was a scholar in history and Indology who studied at the East India Company College and Balliol College, Oxford, between roughly 1889 and 1891.
Patrick Tugwell is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Patrul Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and philosopher. He studied under numerous masters, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught prominent disciples such as Shenphen Nangwa and Minyak Kunzang Sonam.
Paul Althaus was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen (circa 1908–1913). He later held an academic post at the University of Rostock from around 1920 to 1925.

Paul Arnold Irzel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the universities of Strasbourg, Munich, and Leipzig. He earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig (~1887–1890) under the supervision of Ernst Windisch.
Paul B. Courtright is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who held posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University, where he is Professor Emeritus.

Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology who completed his doctoral studies under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He held an academic post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Carus was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Tübingen. He founded the Open Court Publishing Company and edited both The Open Court and The Monist from the late 1880s until 1919.

Paul Copp is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser. He held positions at Western Michigan University, the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, and the University of Chicago.

Paul Crowe is a sinologist and religious studies scholar who completed an M.A. at the University of Calgary and a Ph.D. at the University of British Columbia, studying under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer. He became an associate professor at Simon Fraser University.

Paul Dahlke was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied under Hikkaduwe Sri Sumangala Thera, Ñāṇissara Thera, and W. D. C. Wagiswara in 1900. In 1924, he founded Das Buddhistische Haus.

Paul David Devanandan was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Presidency University and Yale University. He served as professor at United Theological College, Bangalore (1932–1949), and became director of the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society in 1956.
